title: NPS for NRIs: A Guide to Eligibility, Tax Benefits, and Withdrawals

faq.q: Can NRIs living anywhere open an NPS account?
faq.a: Yes, any Indian citizen, including NRIs, between 18 and 70 years of age can open an NPS account. This eligibility extends globally.

faq.q: Are contributions from NRE/NRO accounts allowed for NPS?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs can make contributions to their NPS account from either their NRE (Non-Resident External) or NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) accounts.

faq.q: What happens to my NPS account if I return to India permanently?
faq.a: If you return to India and become a resident Indian, your NPS account will continue as usual. Your status will simply change from NRI to resident, and all rules for resident Indians will apply.

faq.q: Is the annuity income from NPS taxable for NRIs?
faq.a: Yes, the annuity income received from the compulsory purchase of an annuity upon retirement from NPS is taxable in India as per your applicable income tax slab rates.

faq.q: Can I change my investment choice or pension fund manager as an NRI?
faq.a: Yes, NPS offers flexibility. As an NRI subscriber, you can change your investment choice (e.g., from Auto to Active choice) or switch your Pension Fund Manager (PFM) once a year.

faq.q: What is the minimum contribution required for NPS?
faq.a: The minimum contribution required to open an NPS Tier-I account is ₹500. Subsequently, the minimum contribution per transaction is ₹500, with a minimum annual contribution of ₹1,000.
